title: Home boiler (hot-water or steam heating)

parts.label: Boiler
parts.looks: A cabinet or cast-iron box, floor or wall mounted, with pipes going up from the top and a burner or control box on the front or side.
parts.normal: Cabinet closed, no water under it, no soot around the burner door.
parts.abnormal: Water pooling under it, rust streaks down the jacket, soot or scorch around the burner opening.

parts.label: Pressure and temperature gauge
parts.looks: A round dial, often combined pressure (psi or bar) and temperature, on the front or top of the boiler.
parts.normal: When the system is warm, residential hot-water boilers usually read about 12 to 25 psi (about 1 to 1.7 bar).
parts.abnormal: Needle near zero, or near the relief valve rating (often 30 psi). Only judge with the dial face readable.

parts.label: Pressure relief valve
parts.looks: A brass valve with a small lever on top, on the boiler or its supply pipe, with a pipe running down toward the floor.
parts.normal: Dry outlet pipe, no crust at the outlet.
parts.abnormal: Dripping or wet discharge pipe, white or green crust at the outlet, or a cap or plug blocking the outlet.

parts.label: Expansion tank
parts.looks: A small round tank (often red, grey, blue or white), hanging from a pipe or standing next to the boiler.
parts.abnormal: Rust on the bottom seam or the connection, water dripping from it.

parts.label: Circulator pump
parts.looks: A small motor body (often red, green or grey) between two pipe flanges near the boiler.
parts.normal: Dry flanges, no rust tracks below.
parts.abnormal: Water or rust tracks at the flanges, corrosion on the pump body.

parts.label: Flue (vent pipe)
parts.looks: The metal or plastic pipe that leaves the top or back of the boiler and goes to a chimney or out through a wall.
parts.normal: Joints fully pushed together and supported, no gaps.
parts.abnormal: A visible gap or separated joint, a hole, heavy rust-through, or soot at the joints.

parts.label: Gas shut-off valve
parts.looks: A small valve with a flat lever on the gas pipe (often black iron or yellow flexible line) next to the boiler.
parts.normal: Identified only. We never give gas valve steps.

parts.label: Supply and return pipes
parts.looks: Copper, steel or plastic pipes going up from the boiler to the radiators.
parts.abnormal: Green or white crust at joints (corrosion from slow leaks), drips, wet insulation.

parts.label: Corrosion
parts.looks: Orange-brown rust, green or white crust on metal.
parts.abnormal: Say where it is; it is a sign of a past or slow leak, not proof of a current one.

parts.label: Stored items near the boiler
parts.looks: Boxes, paper, paint cans, laundry or rags close to the boiler.
parts.abnormal: Combustible items stored against or next to the boiler or burner.

faults.name: Low system pressure
faults.evidence: A readable gauge showing near zero to about 10 psi with the system cold or warm.

faults.name: Relief valve discharging
faults.evidence: Water dripping from or a wet discharge pipe under the relief valve.

faults.name: Leaking expansion tank or fitting
faults.evidence: Water drops or fresh rust trails on the tank or its pipe.

faults.name: No heat
faults.evidence: Cannot be seen on camera. Needs the caller's words (thermostat calling, boiler silent) and a technician.

hazards.label: Vent pipe disconnected or gapped
hazards.threshold: A clearly visible gap, separated joint or hole in the vent pipe of a gas or oil boiler. Rust or dents alone are attention, not a hazard.

hazards.label: Soot or scorch at the burner
hazards.threshold: Black soot or scorch marks around the burner door or jacket openings. A dusty or dull surface is not soot.

hazards.label: Combustibles stored at the boiler
hazards.threshold: Paper, rags, boxes, paint or fuel cans touching or within about one metre of the boiler or burner.

may: Read the pressure gauge from where they stand.
Move stored boxes away from the boiler.
Show the data plate on the front.
must_not: Open the burner door or any panel.
Add water or bleed the system.

tour.open: Let's walk through the boiler room together. Stand in the doorway and show me the whole room, slowly, from left to right.

checkpoints.hint: Step back so I can see the whole boiler, from the floor to the pipes on top.
Move closer to the round gauge on the front of the boiler, so I can read the needle.
Look along the side or top of the boiler for a brass valve with a pipe going down toward the floor.
Turn to the pipes above or beside the boiler: there is usually a small round tank.
Follow the pipes near the boiler for a small motor between two flanges.
Tilt up to the pipe that leaves the top or back of the boiler.
